meaning: A plan where a company charges you again and again for a product or service.
clues: It has to do with paying for something over a stretch of time.
You may give a company permission to charge your card again and again.
A free trial can turn into this if you do not cancel before the trial ends.
The FTC says a business has to tell you how to cancel before it gets your card details.
Its name starts with S and has twelve letters.
assumes: A one-time purchase is paid for once.
An installment plan splits one purchase into scheduled payments.
Layaway holds an item while you pay before taking it home.

decoys.meaning: Buying an item or service with one payment instead of a repeating plan.
A way to pay back money in equal payments on a set schedule.
A store holds an item while you make payments, then gives it to you after it is paid for.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Try it with someone you trust. Before a free trial, read how much it will cost and how to cancel. Put the cancel date on your calendar.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: A magazine used to arrive on a set schedule. The new version can charge your card, so the terms matter.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: If charges continue after you cancel, save your notes and ask your card company for help.

sources.name: FTC, free trials, auto-renewals, and negative option subscriptions
